title: The Region 6 Wrap: M&F's Optus Vote, Caribbean Exports, Freight Fees | Across the Water, Ep. 5
lede: The week of Nov 2 in the business of the African diaspora: M&F Bancorp shareholders approve a $105 million sale to Optus, Caribbean exports jump 19.1% on Guyana and Suriname, Caribbean business asks Washington to keep its shipping-fee exemption, Ian Thomas tops Britain's 2027 Powerlist as the Bank of England raises rates, and Brazil pauses its rate cuts. Plus Caribbean currencies and the latest Black unemployment rate.
keyPoints: Nearly 74% of M&F Bancorp's shares entitled to vote approved the $105M all-cash sale to Optus on Nov 4 (preliminary); four regulators still must sign off, with closing targeted by year-end (American Banker).
Caribbean goods exports rose 19.1% in the first half of 2026, driven almost entirely by Guyana and Suriname; Guyana was 62% of Caribbean exports in 2025 (IDB, Kaieteur News).

The CARICOM Private Sector Organisation asked the US on Oct 29 to make permanent the region's exemption from port fees on Chinese-built ships; carriers serving CARICOM fell from more than 15 to five (Jamaica Observer).
The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on Nov 5, 8–1; Brazil held its Selic at 13.75% on Nov 4 after five cuts (Sovereign Magazine, Rio Times).
US Black unemployment was 7.0% in September vs 3.6% for white workers; the October report is due Nov 6 (BLS).
